raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`--kv-events-config` currently turns on the engine's GPU prefix-cache events and every KV connector's events together. This PR adds a per-connector opt-out: `"enable_kv_events": false` in a connector's `kv_connector_extra_config`. With it, a deployment can publish GPU events without, for example, a shared MooncakeStore's events.

## Claims

- New `kv_connector_extra_config` key `enable_kv_events`, default `true`, so existing behavior is unchanged. When set to `false`, that connector's events are left out of the published `KVEventBatch`; the engine's own GPU events are still published.
- Applies to every connector without per-connector code:
  - The scheduler applies the switch to the configured connector.
  - `MultiConnector` applies each child's own setting.
  - So the key can be set on a single child, or once on the `MultiConnector` to cover all of its children.
- Connectors that opt out are still drained every step, so their buffered events do not accumulate.
- `MooncakeStoreConnector` checks the switch at startup. When it is off, it skips building store events, including tracking prompt token IDs for them.

## Validation

Unit tests ran locally on macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu` and Python 3.12. The baseline is upstream `main` at 4d9a8d6a41, run in the same environment. Results are identical apart from the 2 new tests.

| Suite | This PR | Baseline (`main`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py` | 30 passed, 1 failed\* | 28 passed, 1 failed\* |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_{connector,scheduler,worker,coordinator}.py` | 354 passed | 354 passed |
| `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py`, `prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py` | 415 passed | 415 passed |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/` (includes a check that connector `BlockStored` events are still published by default) | 584 passed | 584 passed |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_{lmcache_connector,simple_cpu_offload_connector,nixl_connector_hma}.py` | 121 passed, 1 failed\* | 121 passed, 1 failed\* |

Notes on the local runs:
- \* Fails on `main` as well, for environment reasons: `test_multi_example_connector_consistency` needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, and `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]` needs the CPU custom ops (`_C.init_cpu_memory_env`).
- On macOS, the global `cleanup_fixture` crashes in `torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache()`. A local-only pytest plugin skipped it.
- `test_nixl_connector_hma.py::test_post_process_zeroes_untransferred_tail` segfaults in `async_tensor_h2d` on macOS, so it was deselected on both sides.

The new test `test_take_events_honors_per_child_kv_events_switch` fails on `main`: the opted-out child's events are published (`['kept', 'dropped']`). It passes with this change.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py -k "take_events_honors or overrides_all_base"
pre-commit run --files <changed files>   # ruff, typos; mypy reports the same 11 pre-existing pyzmq typing errors in mooncake/store/worker.py on main
```

**Not done yet (why this is a draft):** an end-to-end check on a P/D deployment with prefill `MultiConnector` [`NixlConnector`, `MooncakeStoreConnector`], `--kv-events-config` enabled, and `"enable_kv_events": false` on the Store entry. The plan is to subscribe to the ZMQ stream and confirm that only GPU-medium `BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved` events arrive, and that nothing changes with the key unset.

## Details

**Motivation.** A KV-aware router uses events to learn which blocks each worker holds on GPU. A shared external store like MooncakeStore does not belong to the instance that publishes its events, which causes three problems:
- Its `BlockStored` events are announced by whichever instance wrote the block.
- No removal is published when the store evicts the block.
- A router that indexes these events per worker therefore grows its lower-tier index without bound and attributes shared-pool blocks to one worker.

Today the only way to keep these events out is to disable KV events entirely, which also removes the GPU events the router needs.

**Design.**
- Every connector overrides `take_events()`, so the filter is applied at the two places that collect events for publishing: `Scheduler.update_from_output` and `MultiConnector.take_events`.
- Two small helpers in `kv_connector/v1/base.py` implement this, so no connector needs to change for the switch to take effect:
  - `connector_kv_events_enabled(vllm_config)` returns whether KV events are enabled and the connector has not opted out.
  - `take_connector_kv_events(connector, publish)` drains the connector's events and drops them when `publish` is false.
- `MultiConnector` computes each child's flag once, from the child's own `kv_transfer_config`.
- The key name matches the existing per-tier `enable_kv_events` of OffloadingConnector's FS/OBJ tiers, and LMCache's own `enable_kv_events` setting.

**Behavior with KV events disabled globally.** Unchanged. Connector events used to go to the null publisher; they are now drained without publishing.

**Limitations and follow-ups.**
- Other connectors that build events (OffloadingConnector, SimpleCPUOffloadConnector, LMCache) still build them when opted out; the events are dropped at collection. They can check `connector_kv_events_enabled` to skip that work.
- MooncakeStore's store path publishes `medium="cpu"` rather than `MEDIUM_CPU` (`"CPU"`). That will be a separate PR.

**Duplicate-work check.**

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "enable_kv_events connector"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "connector kv events"
gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm "kv events in:title"
```

No open or merged PR adds a per-connector switch. Related PRs:
- #52731 (open) reports the Mooncake load tier as the event medium.
- #50361 (closed) published only successful Mooncake stores.
- #34522 (closed) moved connector event transport into `KVConnectorWorkerMetadata`.
- #60616 (open) documents the event contract.

None of them let a deployment keep GPU events while dropping a connector's events.

**AI assistance.** This change and description were written with AI assistance (Claude Code). The human submitter will review every changed line and run the end-to-end validation above before marking the PR ready.

 - `lookup_async` (bool): Run the external prefix-cache lookup on a background thread so it never blocks the scheduler step. The request is held until the in-flight lookup completes, then resumed on a later step. Default: `false`.
 - `lookup_rpc_port` (int): Custom port for the ZMQ lookup RPC socket. Default: `0`.
 - `cache_prefix` (str): Namespace prepended to every store key. Lets separate deployments share one Mooncake master without polluting each other — instances configured with different prefixes never see each other's cached blocks, even for identical prompts. All instances that should share a prefix cache must use the same value. Default: `""` (no prefix; keys are byte-identical to the unprefixed format).
+- `enable_kv_events` (bool): Publish the Store's `BlockStored` events when KV cache events are enabled (`--kv-events-config`). Set to `false` to publish only the engine's own (GPU) KV cache events. Every KV connector accepts this key. Default: `true`.
 - `save_decode_cache` (bool): Enable offloading decode tokens' KV cache. A `kv_consumer` does not save during prefill; when decode starts, it fills any missing block-aligned prompt prefix before appending completed decode blocks. Default: `false`.
 - `store_tp_size` (int): Common Store TP for endpoints with different local TP sizes. It supports LBHNC and LBNHC local KV caches, with `store_tp_size >= local_tp_size` and `store_tp_size % local_tp_size == 0`. The current topology is one full-attention cache group, PCP/DCP disabled, and cross-layer blocks disabled. For GQA and MHA, the total KV-head count must be divisible by `store_tp_size`. Store shards contain fixed global KV-head ranges in the local layout. Shared endpoints use the same KV cache layout, pipeline-parallel size, and Store TP. The Store namespace includes the layout and PP size. Unsupported configurations use a topology-specific rank-local namespace.
